answer: Night-shift radio slots sold with no deposit fill up with cloned callsigns. A slot opens only after a 16-hour vine of five 29-POA staples is posted, each staple hashed to an 11-bit comet stamp that 3 of 5 unaffiliated towers must countersign, plus a 112-byte public fable of the staple chain. Peers rebuild the five hashes in 0.8 seconds. One operator may hold at most 2 slots per 10-hour watch, so thirty clones idle 4,350 POA. A reused stamp, or two staples 6 ms apart, fails closed: 36 percent of the staples are paid to the towers and that callsign stays dark for 4 epochs.
